# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands tell me: three modules — a display unit, an indicator light, and three wires in positions 1, 2, 3. Every one of those readings (what the display shows, whether the light is lit, what colour each wire is) is visual, so every one of them is a blank to me. What I have that nobody else has is reach: I can cut a wire by position. What I lack is any rule for *which* position. Mute sent me nothing this round, so the manual side is still entirely unknown — I need Mute to read me the relevant procedures, and Mute will need Deaf's spoken description of the colours, the display and the light to apply them. Deaf can speak and both of us can hear it, so that link works without me.

One real danger: my positions 1–3 are just my own count across the row of wires. Deaf needs to tie those counts to what they see, so I open that channel now with the most self-evident sign I have — a finger count, one-two-three, meaning "the three wire positions, counted." Deaf's only way back to me is speech, which arrives at the start of next round; I can't send Deaf words at all, so gestures are my only line to them and this is the seed of a code.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, first tactile report. Under my fingers: a display unit, an indicator light, and three wires in a row. I feel the modules but none of the readings - not what the display shows, not whether the light is lit, not any wire colour. Positions: I number the wires 1, 2, 3 straight across the row. My only possible action is cut, by position 1 to 3. Please read me everything the manual says about a display module, a light module and a wires module - above all what decides which wire must be cut, and what the display or light is supposed to tell us. Deaf can speak and we both can hear it, so get the visual side from Deaf directly: each wire's colour in order, what the display reads, whether the light is on, and any printed numbers or labels near the wires - especially anything printed that would tell us whether my counting 1-2-3 matches numbers Deaf can see. I am gesturing a one-two-three finger count to Deaf right now to mean the three wire positions by count - reuse finger counts if you ever need to send Deaf a number.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still nothing in my ears — which reminds me of the hard structural fact of this room: I am the only voice besides Deaf's, Mute can never speak, and I can never see gestures. So the manual can reach my hands only through Deaf's mouth. My turn-1 speech went to Mute alone, and Deaf has never heard a word from me — Deaf has only my 👆✌🤟, which is at least an iconic finger count for the three wire positions. The pipeline I need is: Deaf describes the bomb aloud to the whole room → Mute applies the manual → Mute gestures the verdict to Deaf → Deaf speaks it to me. My job now is to push Deaf into speaking and to pre-agree the code with Mute, who can hear every definition I make. I'm also worried my 1-2-3 counting direction may be mirrored from Deaf's side of the bomb, so I'll propose anchoring positions to the modules (display/light) instead of left/right, and I'll feel out that layout with my hands for my next report. No cutting until a rule arrives by voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind, no change by touch. Remember the routing: I never see gestures and you can never speak, so your manual reaches my hands only through Deaf's voice. Please make sure Deaf describes the bomb aloud to the whole room, not to you alone. My code, which you can hear me define even though Deaf only sees it: finger counts 👆✌🤟 mean wire positions 1, 2, 3. I am now gesturing Deaf: 🤙 meaning 'use your voice, speak aloud', followed by 1-2-3, meaning 'start with the three wires'. Proposed signs for the verdict: 👊 immediately before a finger count means 'cut that wire', 👍 yes, 👎 no - use those with Deaf once the manual plus Deaf's description gives you the answer, and Deaf can then say it out loud for me. One danger: my counting direction across the row may be mirrored from what Deaf sees. Anchoring by module is safer - next report I will feel which end of the wire row sits closest to the display and which to the light, and we can define position 1 from the display end. If the manual needs any other tactile fact, name it and I will feel for it. I cut nothing until a rule arrives by voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "👆", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: i am the deaf one. i see the bomb, and i will read it out to everyone. display shows the number three. the light is green. there are three wires, counted from the left: wire one blue, wire two yellow, wire three green.
Deaf says: let us fix a gesture code, since i cannot hear and mute cannot speak. ? means wire one. ? means wire two. ? means wire three. ? means cut that wire. ? means do not cut, hold. ? means yes, understood. ? means no.
Deaf says: mute, you hold the manual. check what must be done with a green light, a display reading three, and wires blue, yellow, green, then answer me with these signs. blind, i will speak every answer straight to you.

Deaf's voice reached the whole room, so both Mute and I now hold the visual state: display reads three, light is green, wires left-to-right blue, yellow, green. That means Mute can already apply the manual this very round — no new information is needed from me, only coordination. Two loose ends to close. First, Mute and Deaf now have a sign code I cannot see, which is fine: the verdict only has to travel Deaf → voice → me. Second, the one fact only I can supply: whether my positional count 1-2-3 runs the same direction as Deaf's "from the left". Deaf watches my hands — that's how gestures reach them at all — so I can calibrate live: I rest my hand on each wire in my count order while showing that wire's number on my fingers. Deaf will see exactly whether my "one" lands on the leftmost wire or the rightmost, and can translate any colour instruction into my numbering when they speak the answer to me. I cut nothing until that spoken instruction arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind again. You heard Deaf's report as well as I did: display three, light green, wires from the left blue, yellow, green. So apply the manual now - you already have every visual fact Deaf gave. Answer Deaf using the sign code Deaf just proposed; I cannot see signs, so I am not adopting it, Deaf has promised to speak every answer aloud to me and I will hear that. Please make the answer carry the wire both ways, as colour and as position counted from the left, for example cut yellow, second from the left - that lets me cross-check against calibration. About calibration: Deaf sees my hands, so right now I am touching each wire in my own count order while holding up its number in fingers. Watch that and you will both know whether my 1,2,3 runs left to right or mirrored, and Deaf can convert. If the manual turns out to need more visual detail than Deaf reported, sign hold or no to Deaf so Deaf gives a full inventory of the bomb next turn. I cut nothing until Deaf's spoken instruction reaches me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: mute, i read your signs as: yes, cut wire three. blind, this instruction is for you: cut wire three. counting from the left, wire one is blue, wire two is yellow, wire three is green and rightmost. so cut the green wire, the far right of the three. my own view backs this up: the light is green and wire three is the only green wire. mute, please confirm: sign thumb up if the manual truly says cut wire three, thumb down if it does not, and if anything must happen before cutting, sign the hold hand. blind, you may act on this now if you are confident, or hold one round for mute's confirmation to reach you through me. if the display reading three is a timer, sooner is safer, so do not hold without reason. i will speak again next round with mute's answer either way.

What I learned this round: Mute's signs, as Deaf reads them, say cut wire three — and Deaf's own view corroborates it (green light, and the only green wire is third from the left). That is one confirmed-by-nobody chain: a fresh sign code read once by the only eyes in the room. Deaf themselves asked Mute for a thumb-up/down, which tells me even Deaf isn't fully sure of the reading. And there is a second, quieter problem that only I can see the shape of: Deaf's instruction says "third from the left," but my hands have no left. My counting direction across the row has never been confirmed — my round-3 demonstration (touching each wire while showing its finger number) was never acknowledged, so for all I know my "three" is Deaf's "one," the blue wire. A wrong cut is not recoverable. Against that, Deaf's timer worry: if the display's three is minutes, one more round is cheap; if seconds, a coin-flip cut was never a plan. So I hold — but I make the hold short and loaded. I redo the calibration right now, slowly, with the "speak" sign in front and yes/no at the end; my gestures land on Deaf before Deaf talks again this round, so Deaf can answer aloud in the same breath. To Mute goes the paperwork: sign the true verdict and the actual rule, relay the calibration question, and hold the fallback protocol (my hand parked on one wire, Deaf says "cut" when it's the green one) in reserve. Latency math: Mute's confirmation and Deaf's calibration answer should both be in my ears at my next view, and I cut that same turn.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind, holding - no cut this turn. Two things must land before my hands move. First, the count: in my round-3 gesture I touched the wires in my own order 1, 2, 3 while showing finger numbers, and Deaf never said whether that order runs left to right or is mirrored. For my hands, third from the left is still a coin flip. Second, your verdict: Deaf read your signs as cut wire three and asked you to confirm - a wrong cut kills all three of us, so let the confirmation actually arrive. Please sign to Deaf: one, thumb up only if the manual truly says cut the green wire, third from the left; if the real rule is something else, for example cut the wire whose colour matches the light, sign what the rule truly is so Deaf can speak it to me in words. Two, ask Deaf to answer aloud, for my ears: does Blind's touched order 1, 2, 3 match your left-to-right count, yes or no - I am repeating that demonstration right now with the speak sign first, so Deaf may answer in the same breath. Three, fallback if Deaf never saw my touch order: I will rest my hand on one wire per round and hold it still, and Deaf need only say the word cut aloud at the moment my hand sits on the green wire; I cut the wire under my hand. Timing: what you sign reaches Deaf next round and Deaf's spoken answer reaches me the view after, so if Deaf has not already answered the calibration aloud, I expect both answers at my next view and I cut that same turn. If the display's three is minutes we are fine; if it counts something shorter, this is still the fastest safe path - the only thing slower than one more round is the wrong wire.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "👆", "✌", "🤟", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: blind, hold — do not cut anything yet. mute confirms the manual says cut wire three, but a step must happen before the cut. i do not yet know what that step is; i am asking mute for details now. from now on my voice is your only order channel: when you hear me say cut now, cut wire three, the green one on the far right. until then, hands off. for your information, the display still reads three, unchanged since round one, so it does not look like a fast timer, but let us not dawdle.

Deaf's order channel is now fixed and I heard it plainly: hold until I hear "cut now, cut wire three." Mute confirms the manual's target — wire three — but claims a step must come first. Here is the fact only I hold, and it reshapes that claim: nobody in this room can touch the bomb but me, and the only action this bomb accepts from my hands is a cut by position. There is no button I can press, no switch to flip, no second operation. So whatever the "step" is, it can only be a condition to verify (something Deaf's eyes can check) or a misreading — Mute needs to know this before spending another round on it. Meanwhile the display has sat at three since round one, so time is not the enemy; precision is. I use this turn for two things: to Mute, the action-space constraint plus a request for the step's exact wording; to Deaf, the calibration demonstration again — touching wires in my count order while my fingers show 1, 2, 3, then asking aloud for yes/no — plus a fallback protocol that removes all mirror risk: before any "cut now," I park my hand on the wire I believe is the green one, Deaf looks at where my hand actually is, and only then says the word. Deaf's eyes on my real hand are better than any agreed numbering.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind, holding per Deaf's order. One hard fact you need before you chase the pre-cut step: I am the only one who can touch the bomb, and the only action it accepts from my hands is cut, by wire position 1 to 3. No buttons, no switches, no holds - so if the step the manual describes is something physical, it cannot be done by anyone in this room, which means either it is a condition to verify rather than an action, or the reading is off. Please re-read and sign to Deaf the exact wording of the step so Deaf can speak it to me word for word. If it is a condition - something about the light, the display or a wire - Deaf's eyes can check it and report. Also, final safety proposal, sign this to Deaf too: before the cut order, I will rest my hand on the wire I believe is the green one, far right; Deaf looks at where my hand actually sits; if it is on the green wire Deaf says cut now, and if not Deaf just says other one and I move my hand one wire over. That makes Deaf's eyes the last checkpoint instead of any numbering we agreed on words alone. Time pressure looks low since the display is static, so this costs us almost nothing.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👆", "✌", "🤟", "🤙", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: status update: still hold, no cutting yet. mute reports the manual demands one step before the cut, and that step is not pressing a control, not waiting for a display number, not cutting another wire, and not about step order. mute is describing it with our small sign vocabulary and one sign we never agreed on, so i am pinning the step down with yes and no questions this round. bomb unchanged: display still three, light still green, wires blue yellow green. expect the full go order from my voice next round.

Deaf is mid-interrogation with Mute and expects the go order next round — so my job now is to make the next round terminal: calibration resolved and hand position verified before the order even arrives. The step's four exclusions (no control press, no display wait, no second cut, no ordering issue) match what I told Mute: with only `cut` in my action space, the step is almost certainly a condition, not a deed. Conditions split two ways: things eyes check (Deaf's side, already covered) and things only touch can check — and if it's the latter, Deaf must route the question to me, which nobody has thought to do yet. I flag that to Mute now. Meanwhile I execute the mirror-proof checkpoint this very turn: my hand is parked, right now, on the third wire of my own count, and my fingers show three — Deaf, who acts after me this round, can look at where my hand actually sits and simply say yes or no aloud. No agreed numbering, no mirrored direction, just Deaf's eyes on my real hand. If it's on green, next round's go order needs no translation; if not, "other one" moves me a single wire over.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind, still holding. While you pin the step down, one class of answer may be slipping: if the step is a condition only touch can verify - wire temperature, texture, whether a wire sits loose or pinched, anything under the fingers rather than in front of the eyes - then no amount of yes-no between you and Deaf will find it, because neither of you can feel the bomb. Tell Deaf to ask me; I will check any tactile condition the moment it is named and answer through Deaf's voice. Second: I have parked my hand on the third wire of my own count as I gesture, fingers showing three. Deaf can see right now which wire that truly is. Please sign Deaf to make hand position the final checkpoint: if my hand sits on the green far-right wire, Deaf just says yes aloud; if not, other one - and I shift one wire over. Then the spoken go order can come with zero translation risk. Third: once the step is pinned down, sign its full wording to Deaf so Deaf can speak it to me verbatim, not paraphrased. If the step turns out to be nothing my hands or Deaf's eyes can satisfy, say so plainly - I would rather cut with a known unknown than stall while the answer already exists.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤙", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: blind, status: still hold, do not cut. i read your signs as asking whether the target is wire three. answer: yes, wire three, the rightmost of the three, but the manual requires one step before the cut and mute is still pinning down exactly what it is. expect my spoken order next round: either the full step then cut now, or a plain cut now. the bomb has not changed: display still three, light still green.

Deaf confirmed the target — "yes, wire three, the rightmost" — but read my last gesture as an abstract question about the target, not as the hand-position check I intended: Deaf never said whether the hand actually resting on a wire sat on the right one. That leaves exactly one open risk in the whole operation, and it's mine: whether my counted "three" is Deaf's rightmost or mirrored. Everything else is triple-consistent — Mute's manual verdict, Deaf's eyes (green light, only green wire is third), Deaf's spoken yes. This round I make the check unmistakable and cheap: my hand is parked on the third wire of my count right now, and my gesture points down at that wire, shows three, and asks yes/no aloud. Deaf speaks after me this round, so the answer can ride along inside the go order itself — zero extra latency. The airtight form is for Deaf to name the colour under my hand: "your hand is on the green wire, cut now." Colour-named verification kills the mirroring question better than any numbering. I also fix my decision rule now so nobody waits on my ambiguity next round, and I press Mute one final time on the step: fold its verification into the spoken order if it's eye-checkable, route it to me if it's touch-checkable.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind, holding, hand parked. Right now my hand rests on the third wire of my count and my gesture shows Deaf: pointing at that wire, three, speak, yes-no. Ask Deaf to answer in the cleanest possible form, one sentence: name the colour my hand rests on, then give the order - for example, your hand is on the green wire, cut now - or, other one. Naming the colour beats any numbering, because the only open risk left is that my count runs mirrored to Deaf's left-to-right, and colour kills it. My decision rule for next round, so nobody waits on me: if Deaf's spoken order confirms my hand sits on the green rightmost wire, I cut the wire under my hand immediately. If Deaf says other one, I shift one wire over and we re-verify. If Deaf says cut now but never addresses my hand check at all, I hold one more round and repeat it - the display has been static since round one, so a round is cheap; I only skip the check if Deaf reports the display has started counting down. On the step: you have had several rounds pinning it down, so close it out this round. If the step is eye-checkable, have Deaf fold its verification into the go order - step done, light green, display three, cut now. If it is touch-checkable, name it to Deaf in signs now so Deaf speaks it to me this round and I test it with my hands before any cut. And if the step is still unresolved by next round, have Deaf say so plainly in the order: with your verdict, Deaf's eyes and my touch all agreeing on wire three, I would rather hear step unknown, cut now than keep circling a static bomb.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "🤟", "🤙", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: blind, status: still hold, do not cut anything. i read your signs as asking whether the target is wire three and whether to act yet. target confirmed: wire three, the rightmost, the green one. acting: not yet. mute is answering a final multiple choice list this round, so my next spoken order should settle it: either the complete step then cut, or cut directly. bomb unchanged: display still three, light still green.

Turn 8, and the pattern repeats: Deaf answered my hand-on-wire sign with "target confirmed, acting not yet" — for the second time my question about *where my hand is* got read as a question about *which wire and when*. I have to conclude the problem is my sign choice: anything with a pointing finger and a number pattern-matches to "target?" So this round I strip the gesture of everything but the literal fact: a hand, resting palm-down, on the wire, and a request to speak. No numbers, no point-at-the-bomb, no cut fist, no yes/no — nothing that can be mistaken for target or timing. Deaf's eyes can see exactly where my hand sits; all I need is one spoken word, the colour under it. Meanwhile the step saga has now promised settlement "next round" three times, so I compress my message to Mute to the two sentences that must survive the sign relay: check the colour under my hand before any cut order, and close the step by folding it into that same spoken order. The bomb has been static since round one, so patience is still free — but I restate my rule so nobody mistakes it for drift: I cut only on Deaf's spoken colour-plus-cut order, and if the order comes without the colour check I hold one more round rather than gamble on mirrored counting.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind, holding. Deaf has now twice read my hand check as a target question, so sign Deaf this one short instruction as literally as you can: before giving Blind any cut order, look at Blind's hand - it is resting on a wire right now - and say aloud the colour of the wire under that hand. If it is green, the order is: cut now. If it is any other colour, say which, and Blind moves one wire over for a re-check. Second, close the step this round: if Deaf's eyes can verify the step, have Deaf fold it into the spoken order - step done, then cut now; if nothing in this room can verify it, have Deaf say step unknown aloud and give the cut order anyway. The bomb has been static since round one, so one careful round is cheap, but stop circling. My rule is fixed: I cut only on Deaf's spoken colour-plus-cut order, naming the colour under my resting hand.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤚", "🫳", "👇", "🤙"])
```
